subject: Embeddings integration: vector dims, batching, normalization (follow-up)

Subject: Embeddings integration: vector dims, batching, normalization (post-call recap)

Thanks again for the call earlier, Carl — good conversation and appreciate the clear environment/context you shared. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size the POC and propose an integration plan.

Summary from our call:
- Goal: migrate Atlas Search embeddings pipeline from Vertex/Pinecone to Redwood for cheaper/unit inference and simplified routing for multi-region customers.
- Current scale: ~5M vectors across multiple namespaces, typical QPS 200 requests (embedding generation) during business hours, occasional spikes to ~1k QPS for batched re-indexing.
- Primary concerns: preserving similarity math (cosine vs dot), matching vector dimensions, batching/throughput, and index migration with minimal downtime.

Action items / questions for you (helps us prepare a concrete migration playbook):
1) Vector dims: confirm current embedding dimension (my notes say 1536 from Vertex). Is that correct for all models/namespaces?
2) Normalization: do you stored vectors already normalized (L2) or are you computing similarity via raw vectors + cosine at query time?
3) Batching: what's your current batch size for offline re-embedding vs online per-request batching? Any constraints on max in-memory batch sizes?
4) Index provider: you mentioned Pinecone for production. Do you have an export (ndjson/csv) of vectors + ids we can sample for the POC?
5) Auth/routing: do you require mTLS or customer-managed KMS for the POC environment, or is API-key OK initially? Also, do you need region pinning for low-latency inference?

What we can provide before the tech call:
- A short migration guide and SDK snippets for embeddings upload and lookup (I'll attach the migration guide).
- A cost/throughput estimate for 1536-dim vectors with different batching configs.
- A proposed mutual action plan / timeline for a 4-week POC (ingest sample dataset, validate recall/regression, test reranker latency).

If you can reply with the answers above and attach a small export (1000 vectors sample) that would be ideal. Otherwise, we can schedule a 30-min technical session next week.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0124

From: Carl Nguyen <carl@atlassearch.com>

Subject: Re: Embeddings integration: vector dims, batching, normalization (post-call recap)

Marissa — great to chat, thanks for the clear recap. Answers inline below.

1) Vector dims: yes, we primarily use the Vertex text-embedding-3-small which outputs 1536 dims. A couple older namespaces are 768 but those are being deprecated next quarter.

2) Normalization: we normalize on write (L2) before indexing. Search stack uses cosine similarity against normalized vectors.

3) Batching: online path is per-request single embedding for user input (real-time), but for bulk re-indexing we use batches of up to 64 and pipeline them through a single node. Memory isn't huge (we run batches on 16GB instances). We do periodic re-embeds nightly for our freshness window.

4) Index provider: Pinecone in prod. I'll share a small export (1000 vectors) — attaching atlas_embeddings_manifest.csv which contains id, namespace, length, model, and a small vector sample. For POC you can use a sampled set.

5) Auth/routing: API-key is fine for initial POC. For prod we want KMS + VPC peering and region pinning for EU customers.

Two other notes:
- We care a lot about maintaining identical recall; any normalization/float-quantization differences that change ranking will be show-stoppers.
- Cost targets: ideally <50% of current per-token embedding costs (we can share current spend if useful).

I'll upload the 1k sample to the shared Drive folder and ping you when it's there. Happy to do a tech sync — Tue/Wed next week are open.

Best,
Carl Nguyen
Head of Search Engineering | Atlas Search
carl@atlassearch.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Embeddings integration: vector dims, batching, normalization (post-call recap)

Thanks Carl — helpful details. A few technical clarifications and what Redwood will do for the POC: 

- Dimensional support: Redwood's embeddings pipeline supports 768, 1024, 1536 and higher dimensions. We can accept Vertex-format vectors as-is; no forced re-embedding required unless you want to change models.

- Normalization: we can ingest pre-normalized vectors (recommended if you already L2 normalize). We also offer an ingestion-time normalization flag so we store normalized vectors server-side. For similarity math we use cosine on normalized vectors; if vectors are not normalized we support cosine by computing norms at query time.

- Batching/throughput: our embeddings ingestion API supports streaming batches up to 1,024 vectors (configurable chunking). For your POC/sample sets, batch size 64 is fine and should map to a single request until you tune for throughput. We'll run a small throughput test during the POC.

- Migration: for index migration from Pinecone we have two paths: 1) bulk export/import (we accept Pinecone exports) with a short re-indexing window; 2) live sync where you dual-write to Pinecone + Redwood during cutover. We'll provide scripts.

- Precision/quantization: we support float32 and int8 quantized storage. For the POC we recommend float32 to validate recall, then test 8-bit asymmetric quantization for cost/size savings. We'll measure nearest-neighbor recall delta in the evaluation step.

- SDK/Auth/Routing: our SDK supports API-key, OAuth for platform flows, and mTLS for private deployments. Region pinning is supported via simple route config (you can pin read/write per-namespace). For multi-region routing we route by customer tenant and model variant.

- Re-ranker/structured output: Redwood can return structured diagnostics alongside similarity scores (e.g., token-level highlights, reranker callouts). We also support an inline re-ranker call pattern (embedding -> reranker model -> final score) with end-to-end latency tracking in the Console.

Next steps I propose for the POC:
A) We ingest your 1k sample in a Redwood staging instance (we can stand up a US and EU staging namespace).
B) Run a recall/regression test vs your Pinecone baseline (we'll compute MRR/Recall@10).
C) Run throughput tests with batch=64 and batch=256 to surface CPU/GPU tradeoffs.
D) Try quantized storage (int8) and report recall delta.

I'll attach our short migration guide and a script snippet for bulk import. Can we lock a 45-min technical session on Tue 2026-06-22 10:00 AM PT? Marissa, can you invite Neha from infra to the session?

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
